With 50 Days to the Midterms, It All Might Come Down to One Thing
 
Plus, key liabilities could impede the Democrats’ momentum to retake Congress, and Trump draws controversy on trip to Ireland
 
 
DAVID PAUL MORRIS/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

Good morning. 

 

The average cost of a gallon of gasoline hit $4.31 on Sunday. A gallon of diesel: $6.20, an all-time high.

 

A month ago: gas was $4.07 and diesel was $5.40.

 

A year ago: gas was $3.18 and diesel was $3.70.

 

There will be a lot of noise in the next 50 days, as candidates scratch and claw and try to out-AI each other ahead of the polls. There will be plenty of debate about Abdul El-Sayed and Hasan Piker. There will be a lot of second-guessing about whether Ken Paxton was the strongest GOP candidate to take on James Talarico. There will be hand-wringing about Maine, and New Hampshire, and Iowa, and Alaska, and Ohio. But the price of gasoline stares Americans in the face each day as they go about their lives.

 

This, and, by proxy, the Iran War, could end up being the defining issue of this midterm.

 

However, here are important points of possible economic solace for the GOP:

 

1. The stock market is at historically high levels.

 

2. The labor market has shown tremendous resilience.

 
 
 

Fresh off the GOP convention in Dallas, I have an exciting announcement. 

 

We’re hosting a subscribers-only “WSJ Talks: Midterms” event in Washington, D.C., on Wednesday, Oct. 7. We want you to join us. 

 

We’ll give you a firsthand look into the Journal’s coverage of the 2026 midterm elections, and we’ll dive deep into how our journalists are bringing you inside the conversations illuminating American living rooms, assembly halls and the internet. WSJ subscribers can sign up to attend here. 

 

I can’t wait to see you there!

 
 
 

This is an edition of the Politics newsletter, bringing you an expert guide to what’s driving D.C. every day. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

People and Policies I’m Watching

 

Irish whiskey: In a surprise trade announcement, Trump said he plans to rescind the U.S.’s 10% tariff on Irish whiskey.

 

U.S. debt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other administration officials say the U.S. can grow itself out of its towering debt.

 

Trump’s Monday: The president is set to participant in several policy meetings today, starting at 11 a.m. ET.

What I’m Following

 
 
ANNA MONEYMAKER/GETTY IMAGES
 

Trump teed up controversy on his weekend golf trip to Ireland. The president voiced support for Irish reunification, an issue U.S. presidents traditionally avoid. The weekend was supposed to center on low-stakes diplomacy with an allied country and a few days of watching the Irish Open at his Doonbeg golf course. At the tournament, the president also said he plans to rescind the U.S.’s tariff on Irish whiskey.

 

Key liabilities could impede the Democrats’ momentum to retake control of Congress. Republican GOP party committees and super PACs are far outraising their Democratic counterparts. And while the GOP has an unfavorable view in polls, the Democrats do, too. The Democrats also remain fractured over some candidacies, such as progressive Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan Senate race.

 

Trump defends the administration’s strategy of minimal regulation for AI. His defense, and similar comments from White House AI adviser David Sacks, came as the leaders of top artificial intelligence companies endorsed a coordinated slowdown in the technology’s development. The president reiterated his belief that the U.S. must outpace China in building AI, saying “whoever wins AI wins.”

 
 
 

What Else Is Happening

 

• The Republican nominee in the Wisconsin governor’s race, Rep. Tom Tiffany, survived an emergency water landing and swam to safety after his plane lost power approaching a Wisconsin airport.

 

• Ohio regulators are waging a battle to curb the supply of unapproved versions of weight-loss drugs.

 

• Under a set of recent White House-ordered regulations, the U.S. Postal Service wants to press ahead with new controls on mail ballots.

 

• Russia is churning out smart, inexpensive new weapons faster than Ukraine or the U.S.

 
 
 

What I’m Reading

 

• Analysis: Ukraine’s Mood Swing (Foreign Policy)

 

• Cornyn Condemns Railroad Commission Nominee Over UT Fans Post (Dallas Morning News)

 

• The Trump Alien ‘Disclosure Speech’ Rumors Are Hitting a Fever Pitch (Wired)

 
 
 

About Me

 

I’m Damian Paletta, The Wall Street Journal’s Washington coverage chief. I’ve covered Washington for 22 years as a reporter and editor. I’ve covered the White House, Congress, national security, the federal budget, economics and multiple market meltdowns.
